title: International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy Nutrition
excerpt: Oats, Greek yogurt, lentils, low-mercury salmon, eggs, leafy greens, and citrus — practical ways to build balanced plates.
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, a woman's diet plays a crucial role in ensuring the health and development of the fetus. International pantry staples can provide a diverse and rich source of nutrients for pregnant women. In this article, we will explore the international pantry staples that are good for pregnancy and how to incorporate them into daily meals.

## International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy
Some international pantry staples that are good for pregnancy include:
- Oats: rich in fiber, which helps support digestive health and reduce the risk of constipation.
- Greek yogurt: rich in calcium, which helps support the development of the fetus's bones and teeth.
- Lentils: rich in iron, which helps support the production of red blood cells and reduce the risk of anemia.
- Low-mercury salmon: rich in omega-3 fatty acids, which helps support the development of the fetus's brain and eyes.
- Eggs: rich in protein, which helps support the development of the fetus's muscles and tissues.
- Leafy greens and citrus: rich in vitamins and minerals, which helps support the immune system and reduce the risk of disease.

## Incorporating International Pantry Staples into Meals
To incorporate international pantry staples into meals, you can try the following:
- Add oats to breakfast, combined with Greek yogurt and fruit.
- Use lentils in stews and soups.
- Cook low-mercury salmon with leafy greens and citrus.
- Add eggs to breakfast, combined with leafy greens and whole grains.
- Drink citrus juice and eat leafy greens as part of daily meals.

## Food Safety Considerations
During pregnancy, it is essential to consider food safety to reduce the risk of illness. Some considerations include:
- Avoiding raw or undercooked foods, such as sushi and sashimi.
- Avoiding foods high in mercury, such as shark and swordfish.
- Avoiding foods that may contain listeria, such as soft cheese and deli meats.
- Cooking foods to a safe temperature, such as 165°F for meat and 180°F for eggs.

## Conclusion
International pantry staples can provide a diverse and rich source of nutrients for pregnant women. However, it is essential to consider food safety and incorporate these staples into daily meals in a balanced way. For more information on pregnancy nutrition and food safety, you can visit our [meal planner page](/planner) or [read more about prenatal nutrition](/blog/prenatal-nutrition).

## When to Seek Help
If you have any questions or concerns about pregnancy nutrition and food safety, you should seek help from a healthcare provider or registered dietitian. They can provide you with personalized information and guidance to ensure the health and development of the fetus.
